result.summary: Enables the `-Wmissing-declarations` (GCC) and `-Wmissing-prototypes` (Clang) compiler warning flags in CMake. To satisfy these warnings without errors, it marks translation-unit-local functions as `static`, fixes mismatched or missing header declarations, prunes dead declarations, and adds temporary changes to external subtrees.
result.problem: Functions defined without prior declarations or internal linkage risk inadvertently leaking symbols into the global namespace, masking divergent parameter types between headers and source files, and leaving dead declarations unflagged by the compiler.
evidence: Commit 37866eda60 notes a silent divergence caught by the warning: 'The header declared AddInputs(..., bool rbf), which was never defined, while the definition takes std::optional<bool> and has no declaration.'
Commit af30d00a3d notes: 'It was declared locally in guiutil.cpp, so the definition was never checked against the declaration.'
Commit b01b52126e notes: 'These were declared in fa6b061fc1 but never defined or used.'
result.scope_notes: This RFC PR includes [nomerge] commits altering external subtrees (leveldb, libmultiprocess, crc32c) that must be upstreamed before merging, as well as a large mechanical pass making functions static across 160 files.
result.changed_since_previous: Expanded from 124 to 160 files by adding commits that mark translation-unit-local overloads and forward-declared functions static, export test functions in module headers, and add nomerge adjustments for leveldb and crc32c.
result.card: Enables -Wmissing-declarations and -Wmissing-prototypes compiler warnings in CMake to catch undeclared global functions and mismatched signatures. It resolves existing warnings across 160 files by making translation-unit-local functions static, fixing mismatched declarations, and removing dead declarations. Evidence shows it catches existing bugs where declarations silently diverged from definitions (such as AddInputs). It depends on PR 36744 and upstream changes to external subtrees.

risk.why: Mistakes could break the build on certain compiler configurations or accidentally hide symbols needed by external translation units, causing linker errors.
